champion.name: donchian-trend-v1
champion.hypothesis: BTC trends persist: buying N-bar highs in an EMA50>EMA200 regime and trailing a wide ATR stop captures the few large runs that pay for many small losses.

lastEvaluation.diagnosis:
The book is losing on signal quality, not primarily on fees. Gross P&L for the week is already negative (-13.92 over 81 trades, avg gross -0.17/trade) before the $16.19 in fees (avg $0.20/trade = the expected 0.1%×2 round-trip on $100 notional) are applied, pushing net to -30.11 (avg -0.37/trade). Fees roughly double the damage but they are not the root cause — the entries themselves have near-zero raw edge (PF on gross alone is close to 1, PF net is 0.099).

Signal problem: winrate is only 18.5% this week (21% over the prior 699-trade sample — this is chronic, not a one-week blip). Winners and losers look almost indistinguishable at entry: avgRsiAtEntry 52.5 (winners) vs 51.3 (losers) — essentially noise, no real momentum differentiator. The one real separator is vol48: winners average 0.00144 vs losers 0.00079 — losers are entering in nearly half the realized volatility of winners. That means the Donchian 20-bar breakout is firing on noise-driven micro-breakouts in a low-vol grind, not genuine range expansion.

Regime mismatch: the strategy's own minAtrPct filter (0.004) implies it should only trade when ATR/price ≥ 0.4%, but virtually every logged entry has atrPct between 0.0002 and 0.0022 — 2-20x below that threshold — and the current regime ATR% (177.23/79870 = 0.0022) is also well under 0.004. Either the filter is not being enforced on the live path (these are flagged "reasonIn: seed") or the regime has structurally shifted to lower vol than the strategy was tuned for. Either way, trades are firing in conditions the strategy's own guardrail says are "too quiet," i.e., dead-market noise where a 20-bar-high break has no informational content. Additionally several sample entries show ema50 and ema200 within 0.02%-0.3% of each other (e.g. 79647.47 vs 79647.62, 79664.18 vs 79647.63) — technically "uptrend" by the ema50>ema200 test but actually flat chop, which explains the 6 quick "trend-lost" exits and contributes to the 51 stop-outs (77% of losers), most within 2-9 bars (avg 7.8 bars for losers vs 13.6 for winners that had room to develop).

Exit problem: the wide trailAtr=3.0 lets true winners run (avg 13.6 bars, exits recorded as "take-profit" even though the coded takeProfit is effectively disabled at price*100 — this is presumably logged as the highest-recorded exit type for trail-stops triggered above entry). But the initialStopAtr=2.0 hard stop is what's killing 51 of 66 losers quickly — consistent with false breakouts reverting almost immediately. One outlier (2026-09-04T12:15) lost -1.90 net in just 3 bars, a much larger loss than the typical -0.2 to -0.6, suggesting a stop that let a fast adverse move run too far past the intended 2×ATR before filling (slippage on a wide-range bar).

Cost drag: with fees+slippage ≈0.3% round trip on $100 notional (~$0.30), and avg gross edge per trade around -$0.17, this strategy is nowhere near clearing transaction costs — it needs a materially higher hit rate or R multiple before cost drag is even the binding constraint.
hypotheses: Entries where vol48 < 0.0010 (roughly the losers' average) are false breakouts with no follow-through, because low realized volatility means the "N-bar high" is noise rather than a genuine range expansion; restricting entries to vol48 ≥ 0.0012 will raise win rate and cut stop-outs.

Entries where (ema50-ema200)/price < 0.006 are chop mis-classified as "trend" (ema50 barely above ema200), causing fast trend-lost/stop exits within <10 bars; requiring a minimum trend separation will reduce trade count and eliminate most of the quick losers.

The initialStopAtr=2.0 hard stop, combined with weak-momentum entries (RSI≈50-55, no real thrust), produces losers that are cut too close to entry noise; requiring RSI≥55 at entry (real momentum) and tightening the stop to 1.5×ATR will reduce average loss size and hold time without hurting the few genuine trend trades.

variants.name: trend-strength-filter
variants.hypothesis: Conservative: requiring a minimum EMA50/EMA200 separation (>=0.6% of price) plus a more realistic ATR% floor filters out flat-chop conditions (avg ema50/ema200 spread in loser samples was as low as 0.02%), reducing trade count and false "uptrend" breakouts.

variants.name: vol-confirmed-breakout
variants.hypothesis: Tests: entries with vol48 below ~0.0012 (near the observed loser average of 0.00079 vs winner average of 0.00144) lack follow-through; requiring higher realized vol plus order-flow confirmation (taker buy pressure, positive CVD slope) should raise win rate.

variants.name: fast-exit-momentum
variants.hypothesis: Tests: entries at neutral RSI (~50-55, indistinguishable between winners/losers) have no real momentum edge; requiring RSI>=55 for entry and tightening the initial stop cuts loser size/duration (losers currently avg 7.8 bars, 77% exit via stop) without materially hurting genuine trend trades.
